declaration.negotiation_history_statement:
Whitcombe Reyes LLP, court-appointed interim class counsel, supports preliminary approval of the settlement under Rule 23(e). The settlement resulted from successive proposals and counterproposals addressing class relief, fees, distribution, and implementation protections. Class relief and attorneys’ fees were negotiated concurrently from the outset; fees were not deferred until after agreement on class relief. The parties considered aggregate settlement costs, while maintaining separately stated class-fund and fee amounts. This description does not reproduce confidential mediation communications or disclose counsel’s confidential litigation assessment.

The binding settlement provides a $28.5 million class fund and an additional $2 million for attorneys’ fees and expenses, subject to court approval. Payments will be distributed automatically using Brightline’s existing records, with practical fallback payment methods and no claim forms. Brightline has not agreed to refrain from opposing the fee request. Any requested fees that the Court does not award will augment the class fund rather than revert to Brightline.

Reasonable external notice, administration, and implementation costs will be paid from the class fund. An itemized budget remains to be developed and will be submitted for court review; therefore, the precise net recovery to members is not yet established. Ordinary internal compliance overhead will not be deducted from class relief, and administrative savings will remain for members. The aggregate settlement commitment is $30.5 million.

The firm receives fixed compensation of $3.5 million under a foundation-funded engagement, regardless of the litigation’s outcome. Any settlement fee award will be paid to the foundation, not the firm, and will not increase the firm’s compensation. The funding arrangement, fee recipient, and supporting basis for the fee request will be disclosed for court review. The fixed engagement amount does not itself establish entitlement to a settlement fee award.

Counsel considers the settlement fair, reasonable, and adequate for purposes of preliminary approval. Although the action survived dismissal, certification remains unresolved, success at trial is uncertain, and trial would be approximately two to three years away. The class fund represents approximately 44.5% of the $64 million in disputed renewal charges before administration deductions and any addition from unawarded fees. Automatic distribution avoids a claims-filing barrier and makes relief accessible to the approximately 400,000 identified members. Independent fee review, allocation of unawarded fees to the class, and controls on administration deductions further protect class recovery.

Overlapping actions brought by Hargrove Lane LLP and Ostrander Bell LLP concern the same proposed class. Approval of a classwide settlement would release covered claims and affect those actions. The existence of competing cases does not substitute for this Court’s independent assessment of the settlement or the adequacy of representation. Preliminary approval should include review of the definitive release, proposed allocation and distribution procedures, notice, and implementation budget. Final approval remains subject to the required class process and the Court’s findings under Rule 23(e).
